teardown.hook: How Costco makes zero profit on their $1.50 hot dog and why that made them a $400 billion company.
teardown.hook_why: It uses an 'Absurd Contrast' between a trivial everyday item ($1.50 snack) and a massive corporate valuation ($400B). This creates an immediate open loop in the viewer's brain that requires the video to solve the mystery.

beats.said: How Costco makes zero profit on their $1.50 hot dog and why that made them a $400 billion company.
beats.shown: Split screen: Close-up macro shot of a hot dog vs. a surging COST stock chart.

beats.said: Last year, Costco lost money on food, but they cleared over $4.6 billion in pure profit from one thing: membership fees.
beats.shown: Chart showing 'Net Income' vs 'Membership Fee Revenue' with the membership bar towering over the other.

beats.said: The hot dog is a loss-leader. It gets you in the door so you'll pay the annual fee, which has a 90% renewal rate.
beats.shown: Text on screen: '90% RENEWAL RATE' in bold green over a busy warehouse background.

beats.said: Wall Street doesn't value them as a grocer; they value them as a subscription business like Netflix, which is why the stock trades at a massive premium.
beats.shown: Comparison chart: COST P/E Ratio vs. Target and Walmart P/E Ratios.

beats.said: That’s why the stock moved today. Not financial advice. Follow for the real moves.
beats.shown: Final stock ticker screen with 'FOLLOW' button overlay.

teardown.pacing: Rapid-fire 1.5s cuts for the first 5 seconds to hook, then transitioning to 3-4s beats once the 'data proof' starts to keep retention high.
teardown.visual_technique: The 'Micro-Macro' switch: starting with a familiar consumer object and immediately cutting to a complex financial chart to establish authority.
reusable_moves: The Value Contrast: Anchor the video on a cheap, relatable product to explain a multi-billion dollar market cap.
The Hidden Engine: Reveal the non-obvious way a famous company actually makes its money (e.g., memberships vs. sales).
teardown.remake_plan: Execute a 35-second breakdown of Costco’s membership-driven valuation model using the 'Everyday Micro-Economics' technique to explain why the stock outperforms traditional retail.
